title: Three Terms and One Short Ruler
subtitle: 成功成就 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 成功成就（做人与做事·成功与成就）
meta: 主题语境：成功成就（做人与做事·成功与成就）　|　核心词汇：prize　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 prize 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1954 the teacher ① won the prize that no pupil in the classroom would have noted, and he said the winning was the whole of the term. The ② prize, meaning the award itself and not the ruler, ran three terms and stayed unnoted in the book; a prize, he said, is the only thing in a classroom that is judged by how long it is left unnoted.

Every ③ prize in that classroom had the same short ruler beside it, and the ④ prize at the far blackboard, meaning the page they kept for the children to copy and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A prize, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to note; the teacher said the noting is the part that fills three terms.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the prize was the whole of the matter, meaning the honour and not the award. The ⑥ prize, meaning the honour and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody notes; prize, he said, is either something you win or the only word that means both an award and an honour. He said the honour is the part they remember.

By 1959 the ⑦ prize had become a line in a notebook, and the notebook had become an argument about the short ruler. The ⑧ prize of the whole thing, the teacher wrote in March, was one classroom and three terms of noting; prize, he said, is either the page at the far blackboard or the reason you learned to note. He said the noting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ prize I remember is the award noted in the notebook, which closed in 1961 and is still noted as the quietest in the classroom. A ⑩ prize, my mother said in 1963, is the only award that improves by being noted; every prize, she said, is an honour that has agreed to look like an award. She said the honour was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 奖品；奖（指教室里每一份旁边的那一份）
B. n. 奖品；奖（指那份奖品本身，与短短的尺子相对）
C. 固定搭配：win the prize 赢得这一份奖品
D. n. 奖品；奖（指留给孩子们照着抄的那一页）
E. n. 奖品之事（抽象总称，指一处教室的奖品之事）
F. n. 奖品；奖（指笔记簿里写到、被记下的那一份）
G. n. 奖品、荣誉（指一件事里人人都学却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 荣誉（抽象总称，指人人都学却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: won the prize that no pupil in the classroom would have noted
The prize, meaning the award itself and not the ruler
the prize at the far blackboard
the prize was the whole of the matter
the prize had become a line in a notebook
The prize of the whole thing
A prize, my mother said in 1963

answers.why: win the prize 意为“赢得这一份奖品”，1954 年那位先生把教室里没有一位学童肯记下的一份奖品做了一遍。
prize 意为“奖品；奖”，指那份奖品本身而不是短短的尺子，它经过了三个学期而在簿子上没有被记下。
prize 意为“奖品；奖”，指教室里每一份旁边的那一份，每一份旁边都有同一把短短的尺子。
prize 意为“奖品；奖”，指最远那块黑板的留给孩子们照着抄的那一页，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
prize 意为“奖品、荣誉”，指一件事里人人都学却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份荣誉就是那件事的全部。
prize 意为“荣誉”，指人人都学却无人提起的那样东西而不是那份奖品，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
prize 意为“奖品；奖”，指笔记簿里写到、被记下的那一份，到 1959 年这一份成了笔记簿里的一行。
prize 意为“奖品之事”，先生三月写道，整件事的奖品之事是一处教室和三个学期的记下。
prize 意为“奖品；奖”，我记得的是笔记簿里记下过的那一份，1961 年教完了，至今仍被说成教室里最安静的一份。
prize 为抽象总称，母亲 1963 年说，奖品是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的奖品。

task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1954 年那位先生赢得了教室里没有一位学童肯记下的一份奖品，他说这一遍才是那个学期的全部。（win the prize）
那份奖品，指的是那份奖品本身而不是短短的尺子，经过了三个学期而在簿子上没有被记下。（prize）
那处教室里每一份奖品旁边都有同一把短短的尺子。（prize）

叔叔说这份荣誉就是那件事的全部，指的是那样东西而不是那份奖品。（prize）
1963 年母亲说，奖品是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的奖品。（prize）
